project.name: ci-incident-router
project.identity: A deterministic bridge from failed GitHub Actions runs to bounded Codex prompts.
project.audience: Developers who already use Codex for CI-fix diagnosis and want failure context packaged consistently.
project.core_loop: Collect actionable run evidence, redact and bound it, emit JSON and Markdown artifacts, and hand the prompt to Codex on explicit user request.
project.north_star: A failed CI run produces trustworthy, bounded context that a developer can use immediately in a controlled Codex session.
not_this: An automatic code-editing or merge bot

mvp.definition: A failed GitHub Actions run can produce JSON and Markdown prompt artifacts, and a local command can preview or explicitly start a read-only Codex handoff.

complete_product.definition: The reusable action is published, installed in selected repositories, and verified against real failed runs with honest fork and missing-data behavior.

outcomes.name: Actionable runs produce versioned, stable, provenance-bound failure context.

layers.intended: The user gets the same useful CI-fix context that Codex already uses, packaged as a prompt input.
layers.planned: The context contract covers run, failures, logs, pull requests, changed files, provenance, and missing data.
layers.implemented: Node modules collect and normalize the configured GitHub API evidence with fixture coverage.
layers.verified: pnpm test and the repository quality ladder pass; fixture and mocked-client tests cover actionable runs, missing data, forks, redaction, truncation, and rerun-distinct ids. Live GitHub collection is not yet proven.

evidence.note: Fixture coverage for actionable, cancelled, successful, missing-log, missing-PR, fork, and rerun behavior.

blockers.summary: A valid GitHub credential and published or installed action are required for live provider evidence.

outcomes.name: Developers can review a redacted prompt artifact and explicitly hand it to Codex without automatic source mutation.

layers.intended: CI failures become prompts instead of email notifications or a passive daemon.
layers.planned: The artifact pair and read-only handoff are the v1 delivery surface.
layers.implemented: The prompt renderer, artifact reader, CLI, and safe Codex command are implemented.
layers.verified: pnpm test verifies deterministic rendering, redaction, bounded artifact download, CLI preview, and the read-only handoff command. A real Codex session remains intentionally user-controlled and unstarted.

evidence.note: CLI prompt, download, consume, and read-only handoff surface.
Artifact, CLI, trust-boundary, and redaction verification.

blockers.summary: A real Codex session was not started; the bridge only verifies the preview and read-only command contract.

outcomes.name: A default-branch workflow can upload prompt artifacts for actionable workflow runs without checking out the failed commit.

layers.intended: The bridge can be installed as a reusable GitHub Actions workflow.
layers.planned: The composite action and workflow template define the provider edge.
layers.implemented: The action and template are present locally.
layers.verified: Static workflow safety and mocked provider-client tests pass; provider execution, artifact upload, and fork behavior are not live-verified.

evidence.note: Composite action, workflow boundary, and mocked GitHub API contract.
